issue_context.title: drivers: gpio: pca9555 : Add GPIO driver enable interrupt support
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
When using GPIO IOexpander driver and pins are connected to buttons or switches.
The app side has to continuously perform polling for gpios to be able to check if there is any change in the pins.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
PCA95xx chips do have a interrupt pin that could be used to implement callback support.
The idea is to extend the device tree resources for PC95xx compatible drivers adding a GPIO.
The GPIO can be use as interrupt, to implement both interrupt enabling and callbacks

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Create custom app module on top of I2C driver instead of using PC955A GPIO driver.

review_comments: Why do we need this?  Can't the caller just save a copy of the result when necessary?

To be able to identify the pin triggering interrupt you need to always know the last state of input register. Seemed cleaner to always cache it where it was read than depending on caller to do the right thing
OK; I see this parallels existing practice for `write_port_regs` so no objections.

This (and all the material specific to interrupt handling) should be conditional on a `GPIO_PCA95XX_INTERRUPT` Kconfig symbol, as existing uses don't need interrupt support and shouldn't have to pay the cost in code and data to support the feature.
